**Peak demand: 1,324.4 kW at 2025-06-16T08:15**, which is 6% above the 1,250 kW contract limit [data: get_demand]. The plant exceeded the contract in two consecutive 15-minute intervals:

- 08:15 → 1,324.4 kW (peak) [data: get_demand]

Would you like me to simulate a staggered start to see how much of that peak could be avoided?

I have the answer from the plant documents.

According to the documents, reflow ovens must be switched **off** rather than left in standby because a reflow oven in standby still draws **36% of its 70 kW rating, which is 25.2 kW**, for as long as it is left running — a large load that produces nothing [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]. Standby is only acceptable when boards are inside; a properly switched-off oven uses about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-01_reflow_oven.md#EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual > Energy-saving notes].

**Cost in incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20):** RF-02 was left in standby all weekend, using about **1,556 kWh** versus about **346 kWh** normal — an excess of about **1,210 kWh** from a single oven [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

Note that the off-schedule rule only flags this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the saving comes from preventing it rather than detecting it afterward [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

According to the demand-exceedance procedure, here is the load-shed order:

**Shed first:** EV charging (EV-01) is the first and simplest action — it is paused first because it has no effect on production, removing 100% of its load. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

The full shed order is:
1. **Pause EV charging** (EV-01) — 100% shed [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
2. Delay the next burn-in loading (BI-01, BI-02) — 35% [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
3. Raise chilled-water setpoint +1°C (CH-01, CH-02) — 4% [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
4. Lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar (AC-01, AC-02, AC-03) — 3.5% [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

**Loads that must never be shed:**
- Server room (DC-01) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
- Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
- Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]

These are never shed because they are critical to equipment safety and production quality (e.g., interrupting a molder mid-cycle or a reflow oven with boards inside would damage the product or the machine). [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-12_server_room.md#EQ-12 Server Room Manual > Purpose and scope]

Note: I can only read and report this procedure — I cannot operate equipment, shed loads, or change settings myself.
